title: Περίοδος πρὸς Νικομήδην βασιλέα, Periodos to Nicomedes ('Pseudo-Scymnus'); «Землеописание» Псевдо-Скимна
author: Anonymous ('Pseudo-Scymnus')
genre: Didactic geographical poem in iambic trimeter
size: About 1,000 trimeters preserved, plus prose-paraphrase fragments of the lost end
edition: Müller, GGM I (1855), public domain (archive.org scans); Marcotte 2000 (CUF).
ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia 'Псевдо-Скимн' lists no Russian translation. Black Sea excerpts are probably in Latyshev's Scythica et Caucasica (1893; VDI 1947 reprint): unverified.
en_evidence: Roller 2021, Three Ancient Geographical Treatises in Translation (doi 10.4324/9781003030379-3); Shipley et al. 2024, Geographers of the Ancient Greek World (doi 10.1017/9781009194211.022).
value: Gives foundation dates for Greek colonies, especially on the Black Sea, drawing on Ephorus, Eratosthenes and Demetrius of Callatis. Essential for Black Sea and Bosporan archaeology, which has a large Russian-language readership. Also an important Hellenistic statement on didactic poetry and patronage.
ai_feasibility: High. Plain, catalogue-like trimeters. The commentary on toponyms and archaeology is demanding but well documented.
pilot_unit: Prologue (about 140 lines) plus the Pontic section; the whole poem (about 1,000 lines) is pilot-sized
